newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Asper outlines Ten Group float plans.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Asper outlines Ten Group float plans.

text.p: The Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) said on Monday it has been told by Canada's Israel Asper that shares in the Ten Group Ltd television network would be floated as part of a wider discussion about his influence over the network.
Ten, which is Australia's third-ranked network, is valued at A$1.365 billion based on recent private transactions.
Asper's CanWest Global Communications Corp has a 15 percent voting stake in Ten, the maximum alllowed a foreign firm, but recently hiked its economic interest to 66 percent.

ABA chairman Peter Webb said he met with Asper, the chairman of CanWest, and would conduct hearings under oath this week to investigate whether CanWest had breached the Broadcasting Services Act on foreign ownership.
"Mr Asper provided details of a proposed float of shares in The Ten Group Ltd, among other things," Webb said.
"The ABA reiterated its support for an Australian public float of Ten," he said.
